findings.finding: The emit-side loudness mechanism (AC2/AC3) does not specify a convergence gate: it must record the drop ONLY when the suppressed non-epic parent DIFFERS from the parent the tracker already holds, otherwise the alert fires every pass on the common inbound-mirrored sub-task shape (whose parent is legitimately a non-epic that is already correct), inverting the channel's meaning.
scenarios: A Jira sub-task whose parent is a Story/Task is inbound-mirrored to local parent_id; every reconcile pass suppresses the non-epic emit and — without a convergence gate — files an outbound-field-dropped alert though nothing was dropped
A store with many such tickets floods bridge_alerts every pass, training operators to ignore the channel
findings.suggested_fix: Amend AC2/AC3 to require the drop signal be gated on divergence: record (jira_key, 'parent') on dropped_field_sink only when the suppressed remote key != canonical_remote['remote_parent_id'], mirroring the issuetype drop rule, and state that _resolve_local_parent reports the suppressed key via an out-param while the caller (which sees canonical_remote) performs the comparison and recording.
